clue.text: Cleric snapping up dodgy agent's old vehicle

indicators.note: to snap something up is to grab it, so the cleric's word takes the other letters into itself

parts.note: a vicar is a parish cleric

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or shady, so the letters of the next word are to be reworked

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: A clergyman buys up a shady dealer's old motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges the letters of agent, and 'snapping up' has the cleric swallow them; 'old vehicle' is a classic motor, not a worn-out one.
explanation.definitionFit: A vintage car is an old motor vehicle, usually one built between 1919 and 1930.

clue.text: I approach machine-gun emplacement with serious intent

parts.note: to approach is to draw near, so near is the verb
a machine-gun nest is a protected gun position

explanation.surface: A soldier advances solemnly on an enemy gun position.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in earnest means acting sincerely and seriously, an idiom for meaning what you do.

clue.text: Food and drink

definitions.meaning: a drink raised in someone's honour

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both browned bread and a drink proposed to honour someone.

clue.text: Oliver the craftsman

definitions.meaning: Oliver ..., the 18th-century Irish writer of She Stoops to Conquer
a worker in gold, a maker of fine jewellery

explanation.walkthrough: The writer Oliver Goldsmith shares his surname with the gold-worker's trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A surname of the Irish author and the name of an artisan who works precious metal.

clue.text: Mild curse heard during sporting competition — a test

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so the curse sits inside the competition word

parts.note: a cup is a knockout sporting tournament, like the FA Cup
heck is a mild exclamation one might hear instead of hell

explanation.surface: Someone swears gently during a match, then faces an examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' sets the mild oath inside the competition word; 'heard' simply says the curse is an exclamation someone utters.
explanation.definitionFit: A check-up is a medical or routine examination, a test of condition.

clue.text: Swift assault captures prime position

indicators.note: the attack word captures, that is holds inside it, the next letter

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack

indicators.note: prime means first, so only the opening letter of position is used

explanation.surface: A quick attack seizes the best spot on the battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prime' takes P from position, which goes inside RAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid and swift are synonyms, both meaning very fast.

clue.text: Club starts to move against corrupt employees

indicators.note: the starts of the following four words, their first letters, are taken in order

explanation.surface: A society moves to oppose its dishonest staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a heavy club used as a weapon, with a spiked or flanged head.

clue.text: What did one make of the defeated men? It came as a surprise

definitions.text: What did one make of the defeated

indicators.note: a surprise turns things upside down, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A victor asks what became of the beaten soldiers, and the answer startles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a surprise' rearranges MEN plus IT CAME. 'men' also finishes the definition's question in the surface, but its letters belong to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To make mincemeat of a defeated opponent is an idiom for thrashing them utterly.

clue.text: Sorceress left out of restricted group

indicators.note: the letter is taken out of the group word

parts.note: a circle is an exclusive set of people

explanation.surface: A witch is excluded from an exclusive clique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out of' removes L from CIRCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Circe is the enchantress of Greek myth who turned Odysseus's men into pigs.

clue.text: Old Secretary of State has not succeeded — about time to retire, in general

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened name goes round the next piece
has not means lacking, so the letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: John Foster Dulles was US Secretary of State under Eisenhower
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the time word is read backwards

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A former statesman has failed, and it's nearly time he stood down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has not' drops the final S from the statesman's name; 'to retire' turns the time word backwards, and 'about' wraps the shortened name round it. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles de Gaulle was the French general who led the Free French in World War II.

clue.text: Peter shot in store

parts.note: Peter Pan, J. M. Barrie's boy who never grew up
a shot is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: Someone named Peter was gunned down inside a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry is a small room or cupboard where food is stored.

clue.text: Free deserter arrested by soldiers

indicators.note: being arrested is being held, so the deserter word sits inside the soldiers' word

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a rat is someone who deserts, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A runaway soldier is released after being caught by troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrested by' means held inside, so the deserter sits within the American soldiers. The page's clue number 11 was misread as part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis is Latin-derived for without charge, synonymous with free of cost.

clue.text: Move boat about before getting something to eat

indicators.note: about means around, so the boat word goes around the next word

parts.note: to kedge is to move a vessel by hauling on a small anchor
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Sailors shift their vessel before sitting down to a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the boat-moving verb round the archaic word for before; 'getting' is a link, and 'about' is not the usual RE here.
explanation.definitionFit: Kedgeree is a dish of flaked smoked fish, rice and eggs, a breakfast food.

clue.text: Worker's loud complaint

parts.note: a worker bee; the possessive 's adds no letter
F stands for forte, loud in music

explanation.surface: An employee grumbles noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: A beef is slang for a grievance or grumble.

clue.text: Kitty meant to adjust seat

parts.note: a kitty is a pool of money, a fund

indicators.note: adjusting changes the arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The pooled money was intended to fix a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundament is a formal or humorous word for the buttocks, what one sits on.

clue.text: I am the heroine of an opera embodying intolerance

parts.note: contracted to I'm
Patience is the title heroine of Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera

explanation.surface: A singer boasts of playing the lead in an opera about bigotry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embodying' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatience is an inability to put up with delay or others, a kind of intolerance.

clue.text: Distinctly defined openings to the right entrance

indicators.note: openings are first letters, taken from the next two words

parts.note: the verb to entrance, to enchant or bewitch

explanation.surface: Directions explain clearly where the doors to the right-hand entry are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' is the verb (en-TRANCE), not a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant means incisive and clear-cut, sharply defined.

clue.text: Body of soldiers not good or chaste

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: a contingent is a group of troops sent as part of a larger force

explanation.surface: A troop of soldiers is neither good nor virtuous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes G from CONTINGENT; 'or' is a link. 'Body' tempts as the landmass sense, but it belongs to the soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Continent means exercising self-restraint, especially sexually, so chaste.

clue.text: Druid comes here for a change he gets none

indicators.note: a change alters the order, so the following letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A druid visits somewhere different, though he gets nothing for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wiltshire stone circle is where modern druids gather at the solstice.

clue.text: Food supply began so differently

indicators.note: differently means arranged another way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The supply of food started in a new way.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosebag is a bag of feed hung on a horse's head, a food supply.

clue.text: Temporary accommodation for wine

definitions.meaning: a canvas shelter put up for a short stay
a deep red Spanish wine used as communion wine

explanation.definitionFit: Means a camping shelter and also an old name for a dark red Spanish wine.

clue.text: State ranks as a disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things wrecked and out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A region is rated as a catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkansas is a state in the southern United States.

clue.text: Stretch of open water where a chap has submerged

indicators.note: something submerged is under the surface, so the letters lie within the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone is pointing out the bit of sea where a man went under.
explanation.definitionFit: A reach is a continuous stretch of a river or open water.

clue.text: Hedge beginning to seem higher than usual

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word, its first letter

parts.note: tall means of above average height

explanation.surface: A garden hedge starts to look taller than normal.
explanation.definitionFit: To hedge is to stall or prevaricate, avoiding a straight answer.

clue.text: Person taking the biscuit

definitions.meaning: as in a tough ... or smart ..., a type of person
the American word for a sweet biscuit

explanation.walkthrough: 'taking the' links the two definitions; the surface echoes the phrase 'take the biscuit', to be outrageous.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a sweet biscuit and, informally, a person of a certain sort.

clue.text: More included in order for drug

indicators.note: included in means inside, so the music word goes inside the order

parts.note: the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
più is Italian for more, used in musical directions

explanation.surface: Additional ingredients are put into a prescription for medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' puts the Italian musical word inside the honour's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium is a narcotic drug obtained from poppies.

clue.text: Man leading a dance

parts.note: a man is a manservant, a valet

explanation.surface: A man takes the lead in a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The valeta is an old-time ballroom dance in triple time.

clue.text: Queen taking a gamble when introduced to snake

indicators.note: introduced to means put into, so the pieces go inside the snake

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake
to dice is to gamble with dice

explanation.surface: A monarch risks a bet when shown a serpent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduced to' places A and the gambling verb inside the snake; 'taking' and 'when' are links. BOADICEA is the older spelling of Boudicca.
explanation.definitionFit: Boadicea, or Boudicca, was the queen of the Iceni who led a revolt against Rome.

clue.text: Go round

definitions.meaning: a go, an attempt or turn
a round of ammunition, a bullet fired

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an attempt at something and a single fired bullet or cartridge.

clue.text: Permitted to run, I bring game to an end

parts.note: to leg it is slang for to run away
to mate is to checkmate, ending a chess game

explanation.surface: A player, allowed to run, finishes the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Legitimate means lawful or allowed, so permitted.
